newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND ON BRINK OF VICTORY V PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND ON BRINK OF VICTORY V PAKISTAN.

text.p: Pakistan, tottering towards defeat, were 94 for six in their second innings at lunch on the fourth day of the first cricket test against New Zealand on Sunday.
Set a victory target of 276, the home side was still 182 runs adrift with the last recognised pair of Mohammad Wasim and Moin Khan at the crease.
Wasim was on 17 and his partner 22 with their unbroken seventh-wicket partnership having yielded 34 runs so far.
Pakistan resumed in a perilous state of 46 for five after the start of play was delayed by 55 minutes because of overnight dew on the areas around the pitch.
New Zealand made an immediate breakthrough with the important wicket of Salim Malik, who added six runs to his overnight 15 before falling to seamer Simon Doull.
Malik was on 21 with the total on 60 when he drove Doull and snicked an easy catch to Lee Germon behind the stumps, giving the bowler his third wicket of the innings.
Scores: New Zealand 155 and 311, Pakistan 191 and 94-6.
